title: Filament Module Manifest
description: Normative schema for filament-core-service modules.manifest payload (FR-035). CR-012 (2026-09-03): optional top-level `semantic` block and the `data_schema` reference form, copied from filament-core-service FR-035 CR-003 (agent-ix/filament-core-service#21, revision a77f31e as vendored by quoin 3e842ce; quoin FR-070/FR-073); no new required key.

manifest_version.description: Version of FR-035 schema this manifest conforms to.

name.description: Module name (unique per (name, version, tenant_id) per FR-026).

additionalProperties.description: Inline JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) OR a relative path to a schema file.

edge_types.description: CR-003 (FR-040): mergeable edge-type registry — verb -> {description, category, inverse?}.

roles.description: CR-003 (FR-040): mergeable role registry — capability tag -> {description}.

lexicon.description: FR-043: mergeable concrete-term lexicon — term -> {definition, optional category}. The EARS object-aware vague-response check (FR-042) consumes the merged keys as accepted concrete objects; the engine carries no hardcoded noun list.

grammar_severity.description: FR-048: per-check grammar severity, `<grammar>:<check>` -> off|warning|error. Merged first-wins across modules and layered under a surface's --severity override. Promoting an `ac` check to `error` is gated by quire-rs FR-047-CON-1 (corpus baseline sweep + explicit user sign-off); the engine default remains `warning`.

property_idioms.description: FR-052: mergeable property-idiom registry — phrase -> {definition, shape, optional category}. Merged first-wins across modules and layered over the engine's built-in idioms. The property classifier applies it after the closed structural signals, as a label booster only: no finding is emitted on that path and `extractable` never depends on a declaration (quire-rs FR-052-CON-4).

observable_verbs.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-047, CR-014): mergeable observable-result verb registry — verb -> {definition, optional category}. Merged first-wins across modules and layered OVER the engine's built-in defaults, which stay at lowest precedence. The `ac` grammar's `unclassifiable` and `vacuous-outcome` checks consume the merged keys, so the vocabulary is module data (quire-rs ADR 0009).

vacuous_predicates.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-047, CR-014): mergeable vacuous-predicate registry — predicate -> {definition, optional category}. The closed half of the same judgement `observable_verbs` opens: a predicate declared here is one the `ac` grammar's `vacuous-outcome` check treats as asserting nothing checkable.

verification_catalog.description: FR-001 CR-003 (quire-rs FR-054): mergeable verification-method catalog — method id -> {name, class, definition, evidence kind, applicability, tooling}. Merged first-wins across modules; unlike the other vocabularies a re-declared id IS reported, because two modules disagreeing about what a method means is a collision an operator must see.

ambiguity_terms.description: FR-001 CR-003 (quire-rs FR-056): mergeable ambiguity lexicon for the requirement-quality lint pack — term -> {definition, optional category}. Merged first-wins and layered OVER the engine's built-in terms, so a module extends the lexicon rather than replacing it.

nav.description: FR-001 CR-002 (filament-core FR-039): optional navigation metadata driving the global menu's object-category entry for this module. Declared by five spec-objects-* modules and rejected by this fixture until now — copied verbatim from filament-core's own `module-manifest.schema.json` so the two do not re-drift.

category.description: Declares this module as an object category in the global menu. Its members are the manifest's object_types[].

slug.description: Kebab-case URL segment and category identifier (unique across active modules, enforced at activation).

traceability.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-050/FR-051): the declarative traceability model — which archetypes mint trace ids, which columns reference them, the status vocabulary, the trace-tag grammar, and the column vocabularies a matrix contract and its coverage rollup must agree on. Absent means undeclared; malformed fails module load like any other manifest shape error.

semantic.description: Optional semantic-module block (quoin FR-070, agent-ix/quoin#293; this repository owns the schema per agent-ix/filament-core-service#21). Versioned independently of manifest_version. Install-time rejections are Quoin's; artifact-time diagnostics are Quire's.

contract_version.description: Semantic-module contract version; 1.0.0 for quoin FR-070.

semantic_core.description: Exact @agent-ix/semantic-core version the module compiles against.

package.description: IR packageIdentity (<org>/<repo>), never a URL or ix:// identity.

exports.description: Object-type names published as semantic types; each must be declared in object_types.

imports.description: Imported semantic packages (<org>/<repo>) at exact versions.

targets.description: Values from the filament-core-data declared target registry (generated targets and representation formats).

legacy_forms.description: Severity of legacy Properties forms (quoin FR-074); error requires sweep_report.

sweep_report.description: Module-relative path to the quoin semantic sweep report that justifies legacy_forms: error.

ArtifactTypeEntry.description: Unified archetype contract (FR-035 CR-002). template_ref, required_sections, and variants are REMOVED and REJECTED (additionalProperties:false → 422) — render is gone. Structural completeness is expressed via body_extraction asserts.

body_extraction.description: Locator DSL (FR-035 CR-002). Each locator MAY carry an `assert` facet driving structural validation in quire-rs validate_document. Supersedes required_sections.

data_schema.description: JSON Schema validating the EXTRACTED record (distinct from frontmatter_schema_ref, which validates frontmatter): an inline object, or (quoin FR-073) a reference to the module's emitted schema by module-relative path and sha256 digest. An object carrying schema/digest together with any other key is ambiguous and rejected by the consumer.

Inline JSON Schema object, or (quoin FR-073) a reference to the module's emitted schema by module-relative path and sha256 digest. An object carrying schema/digest together with any other key is ambiguous and rejected by the consumer.

roles.description: CR-003 (FR-040): capability tags this object type opts into.

LocatorAssert.description: Optional `assert` facet on a body-extraction locator (FR-033). All keys optional; additionalProperties:false rejects typos at load time. Deep per-locator-kind validity (e.g. `columns` only on table_row) is enforced by quire-rs load-time validation.

optional_columns.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs CR-023): the subset of `columns` a document MAY omit. Without it `columns` is an exact match, so a contract cannot ask for a column much of an existing corpus never authored without either failing every such document or forcing an invented value into it. The declared order still holds — the headers must be an ordered subsequence of `columns` containing every non-optional one.

choices.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs CR-010, FR-033-AC-11): allowed values the located SCALAR content must be one of. Legal on `section_body`/`heading`/`list_item`/`frontmatter_field`, illegal on `table_row`/`code_block` — the per-locator-kind rule is enforced by quire-rs load-time validation, not by this schema.

column_choices.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs CR-010, FR-033-AC-12): per-column allowed value sets for a table (header -> values); every data cell in that column must be one of them. `table_row` only.

column_patterns.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs CR-010, FR-033-AC-13): per-column regex for a table (header -> pattern, `{field}`-interpolated); every data cell in that column must match. `table_row` only.

Locator.description: A body-extraction locator: a single primitive (object with a `from` key) or an ordered fallback chain (array of primitives).

BodyExtraction.description: Body-extraction DSL (FR-011/FR-033). Wraps a `yield_pattern` and optional `emit_edges`. quire-rs enforces the match-XOR-iterate_over rule and deep per-locator-kind assert validity at load time.

pattern.description: Either an object pattern (legacy `{kind: ...}`) or a regex string (e.g. `section_body_pattern` rules whose body regex is a bare string).

PropertyIdiomEntry.description: FR-052: one property-idiom registry entry. `shape` is the closed FR-052 property-shape enum in its kebab-case serialization.

VerificationMethodEntry.description: FR-001 CR-003 (quire-rs FR-054): one verification-method catalog entry. `class` is a FREE STRING, not a closed IADT enum — this ecosystem classifies by ISO 29148, and an external user classifying by 29119-4 technique family or assurance level must be able to. `applicability` is opaque to the engine: it stores and surfaces the rules and interprets none of them, because deciding which requirement a rule matches is the advisor's judgement.

evidence_kind.description: The kind of artifact discharging this method produces. Method-class-shaped, never per-tool: the suite registry's own `tool` column carries the tool.

applicability.description: Rule name -> values that trigger advising this method. Rule names are the declaring module's own axes; the engine never interprets them.

tooling.description: Example tooling, as documentation. The engine names no tool.

VocabTermEntry.description: FR-001 CR-002: one `observable_verbs` / `vacuous_predicates` registry entry. The engine uses the map KEY (and its inflections); `definition` is documentation. Structurally identical to LexiconTermEntry, named separately because the three registries are merged and consumed independently.

SourceLanguage.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-051): the closed set of languages whose source symbols the extractor reads. `ts` is an accepted alias for `typescript`.

TraceabilityModel.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-050/FR-051): the declared traceability model. Every field is optional at the YAML layer so a module can declare only the parts it needs (reference integrity without a status vocabulary, say), but what it does declare must be coherent — quire-rs `TraceabilityModel::validate` enforces the cross-field rules this schema cannot express.

exclude.description: quire-rs CR-060: model-level path globs holding NO traceable data. A document under one mints no trace ids, contributes no reference rows, and is not classified for criteria — so it scopes every declaration AND the CR-028 criteria walk, which has no declaration of its own to hang an exclusion on. It scopes traceability only: an excluded document is still schema- and grammar-checked. More load-bearing since CR-062, because archetype binding is what lets a fixture matrix mint phantom ids.

source_exclude.description: quire-rs CR-085 (FR-050-AC-22): model-level path globs under the CODE root holding no traceable source — fixture trees whose whole purpose is to contain a tag nothing declares. Deliberately a SEPARATE key from `exclude`, which is about documents and has never been applied to a source file. The two must not merge: FR-004-AC-9 requires every trace target to exclude `tests/**`, while the large majority of a repository's trace markers live under `tests/`, so a key meaning both would delete the evidence tree. Since CR-011 that rule is MECHANICAL, not prose: each item is rejected when it is a bare `**`, opens with a wildcard character (`*` or `?` — globset compiles with `literal_separator=false`, so `*/fixtures/**` matches at any depth), or names the `tests` tree with no literal anchor after it — every later segment empty or wildcard-carrying (`tests`, `tests/`, `tests/**`, `tests/*`, `tests/**/*.py`, `tests/x*` — the same semantics the spec-artifacts-process contract test pins). Anchor at a wildcard-free segment instead (`tests/fixtures/**`, or `tests/**/fixtures/**` at any depth), which stays legal. It can only subtract: a `source_exclude` of `spec/**` neither relocates nor un-excludes the document root.

obligations.description: FR-001 CR-004 (quire-rs FR-053): which rows state obligations — the quire↔quoin contract. An obligation is derived, never authored: choosing an acceptance criterion's verification method IS minting it. Empty means the module declares none, and every obligation surface is then empty rather than absent.

required_relations.description: FR-001 CR-005 (quire-rs FR-058): edges every document of a kind MUST have — the upward half of traceability. Downward coverage answers 'is what we wrote verified'; this answers 'is anything missing', which nothing operating over existing spec text can, because a requirement nobody wrote leaves no trace to follow. Empty means the module declares none and the check is a no-op.

acyclic_edges.description: FR-001 CR-005 (quire-rs FR-058): edge verbs that MUST NOT form a cycle. A requirement that transitively refines itself states nothing, and no per-document check can see it because the defect is a property of the graph. A blank verb would match no edge and cover nothing while reading as declared, so the empty string is rejected here rather than at runtime.

vocabulary_coverage.description: FR-001 CR-007 (quire-rs FR-059): declared vocabularies whose values documents are expected to claim. A bundle can be 100% acceptance-criterion covered and still carry no requirement anywhere for reliability or security — every document individually fine, the SET wrong. Empty means the module declares none and the check is a no-op.

ObligationSource.description: FR-001 CR-004 (quire-rs FR-053): one kind of row that states an obligation. Minting documents resolve exactly one of two ways and declaring BOTH or NEITHER is a load-time error: `target` inherits archetype/section/id from a declared trace target, so an acceptance criterion is not declared twice; `archetype` + `section` + `id_format` covers a table whose rows mint no id of their own (the NFR Measurement and Evaluation table). The engine cannot express that exclusivity in JSON Schema, so it is enforced at manifest parse — this definition permits both keys and quire-rs rejects the combination.

target.description: Names a declared trace_target to inherit archetype, section and id column from. Mutually exclusive with `archetype`.

archetype.description: Archetype whose documents carry these rows. Mutually exclusive with `target`; requires `section` and `id_format`.

id_format.description: Template rendering an id for a row that has none: `{document}` is the owning document's id, `{row}` the 1-based ordinal. A template naming neither renders one id for every row, which quire-rs rejects.

statement_column.description: Column carrying the normative statement — the text that is hashed.

method_column.description: Column carrying the declared verification method. A trailing parenthetical annotation is dropped, so `Test (TC-707)` yields `Test` while FR-049 still reads the reference from the same cell.

criticality_column.description: Genuinely optional: the ISO acceptance-criteria contract is ID | Criteria | Verification and carries no priority column.

parameters.description: Result key -> source column. Carries a metric's target and threshold, a t-way strength, a mutation-score floor — travelling with the obligation instead of being re-parsed downstream.

combinatorial.description: FR-001 CR-008 (quire-rs FR-061): read this source's table as a CONFIGURATION SPACE and mint ONE obligation for the whole table rather than one per row. A new source KIND, not a new mechanism — the statement hash, the suspect link and the `parameters` carriage are the ones FR-053 already defines. What differs is arity: a t-way obligation is a statement about the interaction of every row, so no single row can carry it.

CombinatorialColumns.description: FR-001 CR-008 (quire-rs FR-061): which columns of a configuration-dimensions table mean what. The engine knows no dimension, no value and no strength — a module says which column holds each, exactly as `statement_column` and `method_column` do for criteria rows.

values_column.description: Column listing that dimension's values, comma-separated.

excludes_column.description: Column listing forbidden combinations (`dim=value & dim=value`). Optional because a space may genuinely have none — but omitting it on a space that HAS them mints obligations over combinations that cannot exist, and the coverage target becomes permanently unreachable, which is the fastest way to get a number ignored.

strength.description: Interaction strength t. Rejected at 0 here rather than at runtime: a 0-way obligation demands nothing and would read as declared while covering nothing.

TraceTarget.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-050): one kind of trace id and the archetype whose documents mint it. Binding is by ARCHETYPE ONLY since quire-rs CR-062 — the `document:` path form is retired and a manifest still declaring it fails to load.

exclude.description: quire-rs CR-038: scope-relative globs whose matching documents mint nothing for THIS target — a narrower statement than the model-level `exclude`.

DocumentReference.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-050): one kind of reference from a document cell to minted trace ids. `pattern` is a regex whose FIRST capture group is the referenced id, so both `Test (TC-707)` and a bare `TC-707` are module-declared shapes rather than engine knowledge. Archetype-bound only (CR-062).

expand_ranges.description: quire-rs CR-015: expand a same-prefix range (`FR-001..FR-006`) into its concrete ids before extraction. Off unless declared — the engine gains no behaviour a module has not asked for.

strip_annotations.description: quire-rs CR-015: drop parenthetical spans before extraction, so `FR-022-AC-5 (superseded by FR-030)` contributes one reference rather than two. Off unless declared.

StatusVocabulary.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-050): the status column and how its values class. A value in none of the four lists classes as Unknown.

retired.description: quire-rs CR-015: values marking a row withdrawn rather than outstanding.

TraceTagGrammar.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-051): how source symbols carry trace ids.

implements.description: FR-001 CR-009 (quire-rs FR-062): marker forms binding a PRODUCTION symbol to the requirement it implements. A separate list from `markers`, and that is the design: `markers` mint `verifies` — 'this test would fail if the behaviour broke', which may back an acceptance criterion — while these mint `implements` — 'this code is what the requirement is about', which never may. quire-rs CR-061 stopped `verifies` binding production symbols precisely because a doc comment citing a criterion would otherwise count as evidence for it. A shared list with a discriminator would put one typo between scope and evidence; two lists cannot be confused. The engine reinforces it by symbol kind: `markers` bind only test/benchmark/fuzz symbols, `implements` only functions and containers, so a mis-declared pattern binds NOTHING rather than the wrong relation.

TraceMarkerForm.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-051): one canonical marker form — a statically parseable construct attached to a test symbol (a pytest marker, a Rust attribute, a TS helper call). `pattern` matches the construct; capture group 1 is the id-bearing argument list.

template.description: Authoring template, e.g. `#[trace("{ids}")]`. Present only when the module wants mechanical rewrite suggestions from legacy forms — FR-051 emits one 'where the equivalent marker is derivable', and this is what makes it derivable.

TraceLegacyForm.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs FR-051): one legacy textual form — a bare id in a docstring, a `Trace:` line, a line-comment id, a trace-embedding test name.

id_format.description: Template rebuilding the trace id from the captures, e.g. `TC-{1}` for a test name like `tc741_extracts`. Absent means capture group 1 already IS the id.

rewrite_to.description: Names the marker form a mechanical rewrite suggestion should target, when derivable.

ColumnVocabularies.description: FR-001 CR-002 (quire-rs CR-015): column vocabularies the module's matrix contract and the coverage rollup must agree on. Declaring them in the model makes it the single source, so a contract and its coverage computation cannot drift.

test_type.description: Values the test-type column admits. The module declares the WHOLE list; a consumer wanting the ecosystem core plus local additions declares both, exactly as `observable_verbs` layers over engine defaults.

test_type_column.description: quire-rs CR-041: column carrying the test type on a reference row. Needed only when `no_source_symbol` is declared — the one rule that reads a row's type rather than its status.

no_source_symbol.description: quire-rs CR-041: test-type values whose verification method mints NO source symbol — an agent-behaviour eval, an inspection, a demonstration. A row verified that way can never carry a trace tag, so reporting it as a status lie asserts something its own declared method makes impossible.

RequiredRelation.description: FR-001 CR-005 (quire-rs FR-058): one required relation. `direction: incoming` and `direction: outgoing` are the same declaration read in opposite directions, so this is one definition with a direction rather than two. As with ObligationSource, the schema gates the SHAPE and quire-rs gates the COHERENCE — but note this definition is deliberately stricter than the others, because a required relation's failure modes are quiet rather than loud: an empty `edges` accepts no verb, so nothing satisfies the relation and EVERY `from` document is reported, which reads as a corpus-wide defect rather than as the empty declaration it is. `minItems: 1` catches that in the manifest, and quire-rs `TraceabilityModel::validate` catches it again at load (FR-058-AC-10).

name.description: Declaration name, reported in the finding. Must be unique within the model — two entries sharing a name make a finding that cannot be traced back to the declaration that produced it.

from.description: Archetype whose documents carry the obligation to have this edge.

edges.description: Accepted edge verbs; ANY one satisfies the relation, so a module accepting either of two spellings says so here rather than declaring the relation twice. At least one is required: none would mean no link could ever satisfy it.

to.description: Accepted archetypes at the other end. ABSENT OR EMPTY MEANS ANY document in the bundle — the honest reading of a module that constrains the verb but not the target — so this is one of the few places where empty and unset carry meaning rather than being a defect.

direction.description: Which way the edge must point from the `from` document. `either` exists because a link between two documents is authored from whichever end the author was writing, and two one-way relations would not express it: they are two independent obligations, so a document satisfying one would still be reported by the other.

check.description: The `<check>` half of the `trace:<check>` severity key (quire-rs FR-057), so each relation is tuned independently. A colon would make the key ambiguous and whitespace breaks the `--severity <grammar>:<check>=<level>` entry, so a token containing either is rejected: the relation would run at a severity no flag and no module override could ever name.

exclude.description: Scope-relative globs whose matching documents are exempt from this relation — the same opt-out TraceTarget has (quire-rs CR-038).

VocabularyCoverage.description: FR-001 CR-007 (quire-rs FR-059): one vocabulary and the projection onto it. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no `values` key. The vocabulary is READ from the frontmatter schema of the archetype named by `from`, at the `enum` declared for `field`. Restating the values here would mint a second list free to drift from the first, which is the defect quire-rs CR-015 closed — and quire-rs#162 was filed against a scope that proposed exactly that.

name.description: Declaration name, reported in the finding. Unique within the model.

from.description: Archetype whose documents claim values, and whose frontmatter schema declares the vocabulary.

field.description: Frontmatter field carrying the claim. Its `enum` in `from`'s frontmatter schema IS the vocabulary. A field the schema gives no enum makes the check unable to report anything, which quire-rs reports against the declaration rather than passing silently (FR-059-AC-7).

check.description: The `<check>` half of the `trace:<check>` severity key (quire-rs FR-057). A colon makes the key ambiguous and whitespace breaks the `--severity` entry, either way leaving a check whose severity nothing can name.

justified_absence_field.description: Frontmatter field on ANY document in the bundle listing values deliberately not applicable. A value named there is COVERED, not unowned: 'this is a CLI that controls no physical process, so it has no safety characteristic' is an answer, and a check that cannot accept one forces either a permanent false finding or a fabricated requirement written to silence it. Deliberately not restricted to `from`'s archetype — the statement is about the product, so requiring it on an NFR would mean authoring an NFR to say an NFR is unnecessary.

exclude.description: Scope-relative globs whose matching documents neither claim nor justify.
